newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower after rise fizzles.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower after rise fizzles.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Wednesday after an attempt to rally the complex fizzled with August prices hit especially hard in late trading.

Although cash power values finished steady from Tuesday, forecasts of seasonal weather, rising amount of generation availability and keen selling by Western utilities cast downward pressure on futures prices the entire session, brokers and traders.
"Fundamentally, things are looking bearish," said a West Coast electricity dealer.
July California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down seven cents at $16.69 a megawatt hour (MWh) after erasing a 74-cent gain.
August COB finished down 64 cents at $20.80 after posting a high at $21.50. Deferred COB months were 20 to 25 cents lower.
July Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down 33 cents at 26.49 a MWh, wiping out a 58-cent rise.
August PV finished down 94 cents at $28.80 after hitting a session high at $27.40. Other active PV contracts ended 45 to 56 cents lower.
Asked about the sharp decline in August values, a Houston futures trader said, "The market was kind of illiquid today. I think someone just tried to push it down."
Day-ahead electricity prices for firm, peak delivery at COB rose more than a dollar to $14.00-15.50 a MWh, while those at PV were steady at $22.75-23.75.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at Palo Verde nuclear station in Arizona returned to 100 percent power early Wednesday. The unit was curtailed Monday to repair a feedwater heater tube leak.

A 450 MW unit at the San Juan coal-fired plant in New Mexico is expected to restart Thursday, and a 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired station in Washington is scheduled to return to service this weekend.
A 150 MW hydro turbine, operated by Seattle City and Light Co, was heard shut for a brief outage.

In the latest six-to-10 day forecast, temperatures in the Northwest were called to average near to slightly above normal while readings in the Southwest would run near normal over most of the region but below normal in the far western area.

Market sources said futures prices could see further softening or at least continue to trade in current ranges until there is news of an unplanned outage or a solid direction from the Western cash market.
"This (the futures complex) should continue a slow kind of decline," said the West Coast dealer.
NYMEX estimated 872 COB and 674 PV contracts were sold.
